title: Inside Day
teaches: The inside day as we trade it: a quiet bar whose high and low both sit inside the prior day's, used as an entry tool inside a bigger setup in a leader above its 200-day, bought as price trades over the high, with the stop a few cents under the inside day's low, the buy off if the low trades first, a third off at 3R and 5R and the rest on the trail, and the knowledge that the bar alone is near random while the stock, the location and the market carry the edge.

facts.quote: an Inside Day's high is less than the previous day's high and the Inside Day's low is greater than the previous day's low.
facts.claim: Crabel: an inside day's high is under the previous high and its low above the previous low.

facts.quote: Look for a lower high and higher low on the second day.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: a lower high and a higher low on the second day.

facts.quote: There is no requirement of a price trend leading to the inside day. However, the trend is upward 53% of the time.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: no trend is required into an inside day; the trend is up 53% of the time.

facts.quote: expect the breakout to be in the same direction as the inbound price trend.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: expect the breakout in the direction of the inbound trend.

facts.quote: An NR4 pattern would be the narrowest range in four days, while an NR7 would be the narrowest range in seven days.
facts.claim: StockCharts: an NR4 is the narrowest range in four days, an NR7 in seven.

facts.quote: Because this is a short-term setup, it is important that the trade starts working right away.
facts.claim: StockCharts: a narrow-range trade should start working right away.

facts.quote: After a buy signal, a move below the low of the narrow range day would be negative.
facts.claim: StockCharts: after a buy signal, a move below the narrow-range day's low is negative.

facts.quote: An inside day occurs when today's price is fully within the high & low of yesterday's bar, hinting at short term consolidation before price continues in the current direction.
facts.claim: TraderLion: an inside day is today's price fully within yesterday's high and low, a short pause before the move continues.

facts.quote: It's also best when the inside bar comes on low volume.
facts.claim: TraderLion: best when the inside bar comes on low volume.

facts.quote: Inside Day Setup occurs on January 12, 2024 (4 days after breakout)

facts.quote: Wait for a tight-ranged inside day on lighter volume to print within a few days of the gap. Just above the high of the inside day is the buy stop that should enable momentum to follow-through to the upside.
facts.claim: Morpheus: wait for a tight inside day on lighter volume within days of the gap; the buy stop sits just above its high.

facts.quote: An inside day occurs when the entire daily price range for a given security falls within the price range of the previous day.
facts.claim: Mish: an inside day's entire range falls within the previous day's range.

facts.quote: 2 inside days in a row is an even clearer signal of the indecision by traders as to the next direction of the stock.
facts.claim: Mish: two inside days in a row is an even clearer sign of indecision.

walkthroughs.title: NVDA, January 2024: TraderLion's own example
steps: NVDA, 2024. A breakout, then four days later an inside day on light volume, above a rising 50 and 200-day.
The bar is small, 36% of the mother bar, and quiet. Location first: days after a breakout in a leader.

Failure mode: the break lasts a day and the stop goes. Instead 3R comes in two days. Trim a third.

walkthroughs.title: MPC, January 2013: at the 10-day after a shelf
steps: MPC, 2013. A two-week shelf at the 10-day, then an inside day closing near its high on 0.66x the mother bar's volume.

2013-01-15: price trades over the high. Buy at market, 31.33. Stop a few cents under the low, 30.90, 1.37% away.
Failure mode: the low trades first, or the break lasts a day. Instead 3R came the next day; a third comes off.

walkthroughs.title: VST, December 2023: the slow one and the trail
steps: VST, 2023. A plain inside day at the 10-day in a slow, orderly trend. Nothing dramatic about the bar.

questions.q: What makes today an inside day?
choices: Both ends inside yesterday's range
A close well inside yesterday's range
The narrowest range in seven days
An open inside yesterday's range
questions.why: A high below yesterday's high and a low above yesterday's low. Crabel, Bulkowski, Mish and TraderLion all say it the same way: the whole day fits inside the prior day's range.
questions.lesson_line: Both ends inside yesterday's bar. That is the whole definition.

wrong.A close well inside yesterday's range: The close is not the test. The high and the low are, and both must be inside.
wrong.The narrowest range in seven days: That is an NR7. A narrow day can still poke above yesterday's high.
wrong.An open inside yesterday's range: Most days open inside yesterday's range. The inside day keeps its whole range there.

questions.q: The inside day is a setup by itself, with no bigger setup needed around it.
questions.why: False. The inside day is an entry tool inside a bigger setup. The bar alone is near random; the stock, the location and the market carry the edge.
questions.lesson_line: The inside day is how you get in. The setup is what you are getting into.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on an inside-day buy?
choices: Cents under the inside day's low
A few cents under the mother low
A few cents under the entry
Seven percent under the fill price
questions.answer: Cents under the inside day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the inside day's low, not exactly on it. Never the mother bar's low to give it room. Kullamagi: the stop is always the low of the day.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the inside day's low.

wrong.A few cents under the mother low: That is the named mistake: the mother low to give it room, then sizing as if it were tight.
wrong.A few cents under the entry: That is not the inside day's low. The stop sits under the low; breakeven comes later in the trade.
wrong.Seven percent under the fill price: That is Bulkowski's loss limit, not ours. Our stop is the inside day's low, usually within about 3%.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: An inside-day buy needs the close above the ___-day, with the 50-day above it.
questions.why: 200. Close above the 200-day with the 50-day above the 200-day. No longs below the 200-day is a hard rule.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200, the 50 over the 200. Then look at the bar.

questions.q: The mother bar is the day the inside day sits inside.
questions.why: True. The mother bar is the day the inside day sits inside; the inside day's entire range falls within it.
questions.lesson_line: Two bars: the mother bar, and the quiet day inside it.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A double inside day is ___ inside days in a row, each inside the day before.
questions.why: Two. A double inside day is two inside days in a row, each inside the day before; a triple is three. Mish: two in a row is an even clearer sign of indecision.
questions.lesson_line: Two quiet days, each inside the last. The spring winds tighter.

questions.q: Volume lighter than the mother bar is preferred on an inside day, not required.
questions.why: True. Lighter than the mother bar is preferred, not required. TraderLion: best when the inside bar comes on low volume; Morpheus wants it on lighter volume too.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet volume on the quiet day is a plus, not a must.

questions.q: In our test, inside-day buys with a fixed stop and no trims lost on average. What do they need?
choices: A trail on the winners
A wider stop on every buy
A tighter inside day
Buying more of them each week
questions.why: A trail on the winners. With a fixed stop and no trims the buys lost on average unless the winners were trailed, and 88.2% were eventually stopped. We sell a third at 3R, a third at 5R and trail the rest.
questions.lesson_line: Sell partials into strength and trail the rest. A fixed stop alone loses on average.

wrong.A wider stop on every buy: A wider stop means fewer shares, not better exits.
wrong.A tighter inside day: Tinier is not better. A sliver with its low in the noise is the B- end.
wrong.Buying more of them each week: Buying every inside day is the named mistake. The bar alone is near random.

questions.q: The inside day's high is 50.00. What is the highest open we would still buy?
questions.why: 52.00. The open can be at most 4% over the inside day's high. More is a gap trade, not this setup.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the high is the line. A bigger gap is another setup.

questions.q: A clean inside day two sessions before an earnings report is still a buy.
questions.why: False. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. Hold through one only if the trade is up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Stay three days clear of the report, or wait. A report is a gap you cannot stop.

questions.q: What happens to the buy?
choices: It is off; the low traded first
Nothing; keep waiting for the high
Buy now; it is a cheaper price
questions.answer: It is off; the low traded first
questions.why: It is off. Before the entry, the inside day's low trading first cancels the buy over the high. StockCharts: a move below the low is negative. Watch for the reclaim instead.
questions.lesson_line: Which side trades first decides the trade. The low first, and the break is off.

wrong.Nothing; keep waiting for the high: The low traded first. A later trade over the high is a different day's story, not this trigger.
wrong.Buy now; it is a cheaper price: Cheaper is under the stop. There is no trade there, only a possible reclaim later.

questions.story: Your buy order sits a cent over the inside day's high. The stock opens flat and trades under the inside day's low at 9:45.

questions.q: We take inside days in leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more in a strong group.
questions.why: True. Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.lesson_line: A quiet bar in a laggard is still a laggard. Buy the leaders.

questions.q: A sliver of an inside day, 0.3 ATR wide, with the stop 0.8% away. Better than a normal-sized pause?
choices: No; its low sits in the noise
Yes; tighter is always better
Yes; the stop is tiny
questions.answer: No; its low sits in the noise
questions.why: No. A sliver under 0.4 ATR whose low sits inside the noise is the B- end. Tinier is not better; a normal-sized pause is.
questions.lesson_line: A stop inside one ordinary wiggle is a coin flip, not a tight stop.

wrong.Yes; tighter is always better: A tiny inside day is not better. A sliver under 0.4 ATR is the B- end.
wrong.Yes; the stop is tiny: A stop that small sits inside ordinary noise and gets hit by it. That is the B- end.

questions.q: Buy the break?
choices: No; Red is mostly cash and shorts
Yes; a leader is a leader, so buy
Yes, but at half the usual size
questions.answer: No; Red is mostly cash and shorts
questions.why: No. Green or Yellow for the setup; Orange A+ only; Red mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: The best bar in a Red market is a bar. Sit on your hands.

wrong.Yes; a leader is a leader, so buy: The stock is one of three things that carry the edge. The market is another, and it says no.
wrong.Yes, but at half the usual size: Half size does not change the reading. Red is mostly cash and shorts.

questions.story: The reading is Red. A leader prints a clean inside day after a breakout.

questions.q: An inside day's high is 50.00. How do we buy the break?
choices: At market, once it trades over 50.00
A limit order under the inside low
Wait for the close, buy the next open
In premarket if it gaps over 50.00
questions.answer: At market, once it trades over 50.00
questions.why: At market, once it trades over the high, in regular hours. Our default is a market order as it trades through, and there are no new buys outside regular trading hours.
questions.lesson_line: Market order, regular hours, as it trades through. No limit, no premarket.

wrong.A limit order under the inside low: A limit under the low waits for the very weakness that cancels the buy.
wrong.Wait for the close, buy the next open: Waiting for the close is another way to trade it. Our default buys as it trades over the high.
wrong.In premarket if it gaps over 50.00: No new buys outside regular trading hours.

questions.q: Bought at 20.71 with the stop at 20.47. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 21.43. One R is the fill minus the stop; add three of those to the fill. JBLU got there the next day.
questions.lesson_line: A small stop makes 3R a small move. Know the number before the open.

questions.q: The stock closed under its 21-day EMA this week and now prints an inside day. Our read?
choices: A pause in a range, not a setup
A buy; any inside day will work
A buy, as long as volume is light
questions.answer: A pause in a range, not a setup
questions.why: Not this setup. A close under the 21-day EMA before the entry invalidates it. An inside day under the fast average is a pause in a range, not a continuation.
questions.lesson_line: Under the fast average, a quiet day is a stall, not a spring.

wrong.A buy; any inside day will work: Buying every inside day is the named mistake. The location decides.
wrong.A buy, as long as volume is light: Light volume grades a valid inside day up. It does not fix the location.

questions.q: The full fast stack of the 8, 21 and 50-day is required before an inside-day buy.
questions.why: False. The full stack is a cue, not a requirement. Above the 200-day with the 50 over it is the gate.
questions.lesson_line: The stack is a plus. The 200-day and the location are the gate.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: An inside-day trade still under 1R after ___ trading days is sold.
questions.why: 10. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money. StockCharts: a short-term setup should start working right away.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing. The money has somewhere better to be.

questions.q: A clean inside day at the 20-day with an unfilled bearish gap 2% overhead. What does the gap do to the grade?
choices: Lowers it; no room overhead
Nothing; gaps always fill
Raises it; a target to run to
questions.why: Lowers it. Room means clear air to the next level; a bearish gap or an old high just overhead is the B- end.
questions.lesson_line: Check the ceiling before the floor. No room, no grade.

wrong.Nothing; gaps always fill: They do not, and a gap just overhead is supply waiting. That is the B- end.
wrong.Raises it; a target to run to: We manage by R, not by targets. The gap overhead is a wall, not a goal.

questions.q: Bulkowski expects an inside day to break out in the direction of the trend going in.
questions.why: True. Bulkowski says to expect the breakout in the direction of the inbound trend, and TraderLion describes the move continuing the same way. It is an expectation, not a guarantee.
questions.lesson_line: A pause can resume the trend. So we want a leader in an uptrend.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Size down or skip; honest stop
Put the stop under the mother low
Pull the stop to 3% to fit
questions.answer: Size down or skip; honest stop
questions.why: Size down or skip. A stop well over 3% means a smaller position or no trade. Never the mother low to give it room, and never a stop pulled in to fit the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

wrong.Put the stop under the mother low: That is the named mistake: the mother low to give it room. Room is paid for in size, not in a wider stop.
wrong.Pull the stop to 3% to fit: A stop pulled inside the inside day's range is not a stop. The honest stop stays; the size moves.

questions.story: The inside day is wide: the stop under its low sits 4.5% from the trigger. The mother bar's low is 7% away.

questions.q: Bought at 41.09 with the stop at 40.45. How far below the buy is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 1.56%. The buy minus the stop, divided by the buy. ATI's stop sat well inside the 3% habit.
questions.lesson_line: Trigger minus stop, over the trigger. Inside days give small stops.

questions.q: The inside day ran 20.00 to 21.00 and closed at 20.80. Where in its range did it close, 0 to 1?
questions.why: 0.8, near the high. Close minus low, over high minus low. A close in the upper half is preferred, as a cue and not a rule.
questions.lesson_line: Close minus low, over high minus low. Near the top is the picture we like.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Out; the loss is past 2R
The new stop is 46.70
Hold; gaps usually fill
questions.why: Out. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low, with a ceiling: past 2R, get out. A low of 46.70 is past it.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception, and it has a ceiling of 2R.

wrong.The new stop is 46.70: The 30-minute low becomes the stop only while the loss is inside 2R. This one is past it, so you are out.
wrong.Hold; gaps usually fill: Hope is not a rule. The gap rule has a ceiling, and this is past it.

questions.story: You bought the break at 50.00 with the stop at 48.70. The next morning it gaps open at 47.80. The first 30-minute bar's low is 46.70.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Sell a third at the open
Wait for the close to sell
Sell it all at the open
questions.answer: Sell a third at the open
questions.why: Sell a third at the open. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open. The 3R third comes off right there.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through a trim level is the trim. Take it at the open.

wrong.Wait for the close to sell: The level is already passed. Waiting gives the gap a chance to fill.
wrong.Sell it all at the open: A third at 3R. The rest waits for 5R and the trail.

questions.story: Your inside-day long sits at 2.7R at the close. It opens the next morning at 3.5R.

questions.q: Mish's 2009 AAPL inside-day buy sat about 17% under its 200-day. Would we take it?
choices: No; no longs below the 200-day
Yes; the pattern is the pattern
Yes; it was a market bottom
questions.why: No. No longs below the 200-day, however well the example worked. Mish's AAPL buy sat about 17% under it.
questions.lesson_line: Other people's rules can be right for them. The 200-day line is ours.

wrong.Yes; the pattern is the pattern: The pattern is an entry tool. Below the 200-day there is nothing to enter.
wrong.Yes; it was a market bottom: Bottoms are known later. The rule is known before: no longs below the 200-day.

questions.q: Yesterday ran 52.00 to 49.00. Which day today is an inside day?
questions.why: High 51.50, low 49.50. Both ends sit inside yesterday's range: the high is under 52.00 and the low is over 49.00.
questions.lesson_line: Check both ends. One end inside is half a definition.

wrong.High 52.40, low 50.00: The low is inside, but the high is above 52.00. Both ends must be inside.
wrong.High 51.00, low 48.50: The high is inside, but the low is under 49.00. Both ends must be inside.
wrong.High 53.00, low 48.00: Both ends poke out. That day covers yesterday's whole range.

questions.q: On an inside-day trade the stop moves to breakeven between 2R and 5R.
questions.why: True. Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R; the first trim at 3R is the natural moment.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

questions.q: Which trade is it now?
choices: The reclaim, with its own stop
The inside-day break; buy the high
No trade; the low broke
questions.answer: The reclaim, with its own stop
questions.why: The reclaim. Once the low trades first, the buy over the high is off. Our Sunday Scans name the second scenario: undercut and reclaim, with a stop at the new support.
questions.lesson_line: Two scenarios: the break of the high, or the undercut and reclaim. The low first means the break is off.

wrong.The inside-day break; buy the high: The low traded first, so the break is off. The reclaim is the trade now.
wrong.No trade; the low broke: The break is off; the reclaim is its own trade with its own stop.

questions.story: The inside day's low broke at 10:05. By 11:00 price has reclaimed that low and holds above it.

questions.q: Bought at 55.02, stop 54.28. The stock trades to 58.72. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. By default the second third comes off here.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 5R is the second trim.

questions.q: What was the close, and what decides the exit?
choices: A warning; the gap rule decides
The exit; sell at that weak close
Noise; give the stop more room
questions.answer: A warning; the gap rule decides
questions.why: A warning, not an exit; hold to the stop. The next open was under the stop, so the first 30-minute low decides the real exit.
questions.lesson_line: The weak close warns. The stop exits. The gap rule handles the gap.

wrong.The exit; sell at that weak close: The close under the high is a warning. The stop is the exit, and it had not traded at the close.
wrong.Noise; give the stop more room: The stop only moves up. A weak close is a reason to watch, never to widen.

questions.story: You bought the break at 32.35, stop 31.76. The entry day closes at its low, 31.84, back under the inside day's high. The next session opens at 31.58.

questions.q: How do you read this loss?
choices: A planned loss at a B- spot
A mistake; the stop needed room
A mistake; inside days never work
questions.answer: A planned loss at a B- spot
questions.why: A planned loss at a B- spot. Six up days in a row before the pause is the B- end, and the stop did its job.
questions.lesson_line: Grade the spot before the bar. Late in a run, the quiet day is the B- end.

wrong.A mistake; the stop needed room: Room means a bigger loss. The stock fell to 46.35 within 10 sessions.
wrong.A mistake; inside days never work: They can work. The spot, late in a run, was the problem, not the bar.

questions.story: Six up closes in a row, then an inside day. You bought the break at 49.94 with a 1.06% stop at 49.41. The next session's low was 49.11.

questions.q: What was the tell before the buy?
choices: A stall under the fast average
The 2.37% stop was too wide
Nothing; it just failed
questions.answer: A stall under the fast average
questions.why: The stall. An inside day inside a stall under the fast average is a pause in a range, not a continuation. The next open was under the stop, the gap rule's case.
questions.lesson_line: A quiet day inside a stall is a range, not a spring.

wrong.The 2.37% stop was too wide: The stop was inside the 3% habit. The location was the problem, not the stop.
wrong.Nothing; it just failed: A week of closes under the fast average was there to see. The location decides.

questions.story: The stock closed under its 10-day for a week after a big run. It prints an inside day 0.7% under a flat 10-day; you buy the break at 91.31, stop 89.14. The break lasts one day.

questions.q: Our test bought every qualifying inside day: 101,129 buys. How many reached 3R before a fixed stop?
choices: About one in four, 26.7%
About half, a coin flip
About nine in ten, 88.2%
questions.why: About one in four: 26.7% reached 3R and 88.2% were eventually stopped. The bar alone is near random; the rule set is a filter, not an edge by itself.
questions.lesson_line: The bar is a filter. The stock, the location, the market and the trail are the edge.

wrong.About half, a coin flip: Our test found 26.7%, nowhere near half. The bar is a filter.
wrong.About nine in ten, 88.2%: Nine in ten were stopped, not winners. The inside day alone is near random.

questions.q: By default, the second third of an inside-day winner comes off at 4R.
questions.why: False. After the first third at 3R, the default is another third at 5R, then trail the last third. It is adjustable.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, trail the rest.

questions.q: Buy the open?
choices: No; a gap trade, not this setup
Yes; strength is strength
Yes; the stop is the inside low
questions.answer: No; a gap trade, not this setup
questions.why: No. Buy the open only if it opens no more than 4% over the inside day's high. This one opened 6.0% over, an earnings gap trade with its own rules. The stop under the inside low would be 6.95% away.
questions.lesson_line: A big gap over the quiet day is another setup. Trade it by its own card or not at all.

wrong.Yes; strength is strength: Strength 6% over the high is a gap trade. The inside-day rules stop at 4%.
wrong.Yes; the stop is the inside low: That stop would be 6.95% away. Far outside the 3% habit, and the wrong setup anyway.

questions.story: A clean inside day sits at the 21-day EMA. Earnings come after the close, and the next open is 6.0% over its high.

questions.q: The last third of an inside-day winner trails which line?
choices: The 10-day or the 21-day line
The 50-day, sold on a close
The mother bar's low
No trail; hold it for 10R or more
questions.why: The 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one, sold on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the rising average. Sell the close below it, not the touch.

wrong.The 50-day, sold on a close: The trail is the 10-day or the 21-day, not the 50-day.
wrong.The mother bar's low: The mother bar is history by then. The trail is a moving average.
wrong.No trail; hold it for 10R or more: The last third needs an exit rule, and the rule is the trail, not a hope for 10R.

questions.q: Take the break?
choices: No; not a leader
Yes; the breakout carries it
Yes, as a B at half size
questions.why: No. We buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups. An RS rating of 55 is not one.
questions.lesson_line: A clean bar in a laggard is a clean bar going nowhere.

wrong.Yes; the breakout carries it: A breakout in a laggard is still a laggard. Buy the leaders.
wrong.Yes, as a B at half size: Size does not make a laggard a leader. The RS gate comes first.

questions.story: A clean inside day after a breakout, in a stock with an RS rating of 55 in a lagging group.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 0.25%. Trigger 38.00, stop 37.53. How many shares?
questions.why: 265. Account times risk percent, divided by the trigger minus the stop, rounded down. That is well under the cap of 40% of the account. VST's stop was 37.53.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Which grades higher?
choices: The 0.6x one; lighter is preferred
The 1.4x one; volume is strength
Equal; volume is not a rule
questions.why: The lighter one. Volume lighter than the mother bar is preferred, not required; a heavy, wide, red mother bar is the B- end. TraderLion and Morpheus want the inside bar on lighter volume.
questions.lesson_line: A quiet bar on quiet volume after a loud move. That is the picture.

wrong.The 1.4x one; volume is strength: Heavy volume on the pause is noise, not strength. The expansion day wants volume; the inside day wants quiet.
wrong.Equal; volume is not a rule: Not a rule, but a grade. Lighter is preferred, and the red mother bar grades it down further.

questions.story: Two inside days after the same kind of breakout. One printed on 0.6x the mother bar's volume. The other on 1.4x, under a wide red mother bar.

questions.q: Inside day or wick play?
choices: Both; a wick play is an inside day
A wick play, and not an inside day
An inside day, not a wick play
questions.answer: Both; a wick play is an inside day
questions.why: Both. Every strict wick play is an inside day; most inside days are not wick plays. Where the small day sits inside the big one is the difference.
questions.lesson_line: Look where the small day sits. In the upper wick, it carries two names.

wrong.A wick play, and not an inside day: Its high is under yesterday's high and its low above yesterday's low. That is an inside day too.
wrong.An inside day, not a wick play: It sits wholly inside the upper wick, above the body top. That is the wick play's shape.

questions.story: The small bar sits entirely above yesterday's body, inside yesterday's upper wick. Its high is under yesterday's high and its low is over yesterday's low. We call that a wick play.

questions.q: The mother bar's low is a fine stop when the inside day's low feels too tight.
questions.why: False. Never the mother low just to give it room. If the honest stop is too wide, size down or skip.
questions.lesson_line: Room is paid for in shares, never in a wider stop.

questions.q: Take the break?
choices: No; no setup behind the bar
Yes; tight is tight
Yes, small
questions.answer: No; no setup behind the bar
questions.why: No. The inside day is an entry tool inside a bigger setup. A choppy range under a falling 50-day has nothing to enter. It is the B- end of the spots.
questions.lesson_line: A quiet day in chop is just a quiet day in chop.

wrong.Yes; tight is tight: Tight inside nothing is nothing. The location carries the edge.
wrong.Yes, small: Small size does not create a setup. There is no structure here to buy.

questions.story: A stock in the middle of a choppy range, under a falling 50-day, prints a tight inside day.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: No; under $10 and $20 million
Yes; the bar is the bar
Yes, small
questions.why: No. Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day. The chart is fine and the stock is not ours.
questions.lesson_line: A clean bar in a thin stock is still a thin stock.

wrong.Yes; the bar is the bar: The liquidity rule comes before the chart.
wrong.Yes, small: Size does not make a thin stock liquid.

questions.story: A $6 stock trading $4 million a day prints a perfect inside day after a breakout.

questions.q: In our four failure examples, the entry day held above the inside day's high in each one.
questions.why: False. In all four the entry day itself closed back under the inside day's high. That close is the warning; the stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: A break that does not hold into the close is a warning. The stop is still the exit.

questions.q: Two of the four failures opened under the stop the next morning. What decided the real loss?
choices: The first 30-minute low
The stop order's price
The prior day's close
questions.why: The first 30-minute low. When the open is under the stop, the gap rule decides, not the stop order: the first 30-minute low is the new stop, out if past 2R.
questions.lesson_line: A stop order cannot catch a gap. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.The stop order's price: The open was already under it. The order fills at the open, not at its price, unless the gap rule holds you.
wrong.The prior day's close: The close is where the warning was. The loss is decided the next morning.

questions.q: Buy 50.00, stop 48.40. The 14-day ATR is 1.20. How many ATR is the stop?
questions.why: 1.33 ATR. The stop distance divided by the ATR. The card flags a stop over 1 ATR as wide: size down or skip, and never the mother low.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop in ATR. Over one ATR, size down or skip.

questions.q: Inside day, Kicker, or gap trade?
choices: A Kicker; gap over a weak red day
An inside day break after the gap
Nothing; we skip gaps this size
questions.answer: A Kicker; gap over a weak red day
questions.why: A Kicker. It needs a weak red day closing in the lowest 35% of its range. Then a gap of 1.5% or more over its close. An inside day is a quiet bar bought over its own high.
questions.lesson_line: Check the bar before the gap. A weak red day under a gap is the Kicker.

wrong.An inside day break after the gap: There is no inside day here. Today gapped over yesterday's high; nothing sat inside it.
wrong.Nothing; we skip gaps this size: A gap is a setup of its own. This one has a name: the Kicker.

questions.story: Yesterday was a weak red day closing in the bottom of its range. Today gaps 3% over its close and trades through yesterday's high.
A clean inside day sits three sessions after an earnings gap. It closes 14% over its 10-day average.
questions.q: Take the break?
choices: No; too stretched over the 10-day
Yes; the bar is clean
Yes, on half size
questions.why: No. Skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average. This one closes 14% over it, so the pause came too high.
questions.lesson_line: A clean bar, too far above its average, is still a pass.

wrong.Yes; the bar is clean: The bar was clean. The stock was stretched, and the stretch rule comes before the bar.
wrong.Yes, on half size: Half size does not cure a stretch. Skip the long over the line.

questions.q: What is the inside day here?
choices: The flag's entry, not a second setup
A second setup; two trades
A warning; the flag failed
questions.answer: The flag's entry, not a second setup
questions.why: The flag's entry. An inside day inside a flag is the flag's entry, not a second setup. One structure, one trade, one stop.
questions.lesson_line: The structure is the setup. The quiet day is how you get in.

wrong.A second setup; two trades: Full size at one price with one stop. The inside day times the flag's entry; it does not double it.
wrong.A warning; the flag failed: A quiet day inside a flag is the drift the flag wants, not a failure.

questions.story: A 20% pole, then eight sessions of quiet drift. The sixth drift day is an inside day.

questions.q: Buy the open?
choices: Yes; inside the 4% line
No; never buy a gap
No; wait for a pullback
questions.why: Yes. A gap over the trigger is bought at the open if it opens no more than 4% over the inside day's high. NVDA's buy opened 0.1% over its trigger and reached 3R in two days.
questions.lesson_line: A hair over the high is the trigger, not a chase. Buy the open.

wrong.No; never buy a gap: A small gap over the trigger is bought at the open. The line is 4%, not zero.
wrong.No; wait for a pullback: The trigger already traded, and the gap is far inside the 4% line. A pullback may never come.

questions.story: The inside day's high is 80.00. The stock opens at 80.08, 0.1% over it.

questions.q: Bulkowski found that the trend leading into an inside day is upward only 53% of the time.
questions.why: True. There is no requirement of a trend leading to the inside day; the trend is upward 53% of the time. The bar alone is near random, so we add the 200-day and the location.
questions.lesson_line: The bar does not know which way. The trend and the location do.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.answer: Sell; hold through only if up 5R
questions.why: Sell. Hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R, and this one is at 2R.
questions.lesson_line: Hold through a report only at 5R. Below that, take the money before it.
questions.story: You hold an inside-day winner at 2R. It reports earnings tomorrow after the close.
choices: Sell; hold through only if up 5R
Hold; it is working well so far
Hold; the stop is at breakeven now

wrong.Hold; it is working well so far: Working at 2R is not 5R. A report can gap through any stop.
wrong.Hold; the stop is at breakeven now: A report can gap through the stop. Below 5R, the rule is to be out before it.

questions.q: Trade them tomorrow?
choices: Wait for the indexes to break
Yes; three setups is a list
Yes, half size
questions.answer: Wait for the indexes to break
questions.why: Wait. When the indexes print a cluster of inside days, wait for the break. Contraction comes before expansion, in either direction.
questions.lesson_line: Coiled indexes break both ways. Let them pick first.

wrong.Yes; three setups is a list: Three breaks into an undecided market are three coin flips.
wrong.Yes, half size: Half size does not tell you which way the market breaks.

questions.story: SPY and QQQ both printed inside days today. Your focus list holds three inside-day breaks for tomorrow.

questions.q: Crabel took profits at the close of the first day. Is that our exit?
choices: No; ours is trims and a trail
Yes; same bar, same exit
Yes, if volume is light
questions.answer: No; ours is trims and a trail
questions.why: No. Crabel's exit is the close of the first trading day. Ours is a third at 3R, a third at 5R and a trail.
questions.lesson_line: Same bar, different trade. Ours holds for the trims and the trail.

wrong.Yes; same bar, same exit: The bar is the same. The exit is not: ours is trims and a trail.
wrong.Yes, if volume is light: Volume does not change the exit.

questions.q: Write the plan.
choices: Buy 55.02, stop 54.28, a third at 3R
Buy 55.02, stop 52.00, and hold it all
Wait for the close; mother-low stop
questions.why: Buy the open at market, 55.02. Stop a few cents under the inside low, 54.28. A third comes off at 3R, which took two days.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open; execute it without a debate.

wrong.Buy 55.02, stop 52.00, and hold it all: The stop belongs a few cents under the inside day's low, 54.28. And a third comes off at 3R.
wrong.Wait for the close; mother-low stop: The trigger is the trade over the high, our default, not the close. The mother low is the named mistake.

questions.story: NVDA, January 2024: an inside day four days after a breakout, on light volume. The next session opens a hair over the high.

questions.q: What does Yellow change?
choices: Smaller and fewer
Nothing; Yellow is Green
A+ only
questions.why: Smaller and fewer. Green or Yellow for the setup; Yellow means smaller and fewer, Orange A+ only, Red mostly cash.
questions.lesson_line: Yellow is a go, with the size turned down.

wrong.Nothing; Yellow is Green: Green is full risk. Yellow is smaller and fewer.
wrong.A+ only: A+ only is Orange. Yellow still allows a B, at smaller size.

questions.story: The reading is Yellow. Two inside days on your list, both graded B.

questions.q: Buy again?
choices: Yes; a new trade, its own stop
No; one try per stock
Yes, with the stop under Monday's low
questions.answer: Yes; a new trade, its own stop
questions.why: Yes. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule. At most 3 tries in a week.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a verdict on the setup. The next trigger is a new trade.

wrong.No; one try per stock: The limit is 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, not one.
wrong.Yes, with the stop under Monday's low: The stop is the new inside day's low. Monday's low is the old trade.

questions.story: Stopped out of an inside-day break on Monday. Wednesday prints a new inside day and Thursday trades over its high.

questions.q: A leader breaks out of a base on Friday and you are not in. What do you watch for?
choices: An inside day or two up here
A buy at Monday's open, at market
A pullback to the 200-day
questions.answer: An inside day or two up here
questions.why: An inside day or two up here. The breakout is the setup; the inside day is the entry tool inside it.
questions.lesson_line: Missed the breakout, so watch for the quiet day after it. That is the second door.

wrong.A buy at Monday's open, at market: Chasing Monday's open is a buy with no level under it. The inside day gives the level.
wrong.A pullback to the 200-day: A leader just out of a base is far from its 200-day. The inside day is the nearer, tighter entry.

questions.story: A leader breaks out of a base on Friday. You are not in.

questions.q: Which gets the bigger size?
questions.why: A. Just after a breakout, with clear air and a Green market, is the A+ end. An old high just overhead and the indexes printing inside days is the B- end.
questions.lesson_line: Same bar, different grade. The stock, the spot and the market decide the size.
questions.story: Two inside days, both above the 200-day. A: a leader just after a breakout, Green market, clear air overhead. B: a leader under an old high just overhead, with the indexes printing inside days.
choices: A; every cue lines up
B; it has the tighter stop
Equal; the bar is the same

wrong.B; it has the tighter stop: Nothing says B's stop is tighter. Its room and its market grade it down.
wrong.Equal; the bar is the same: The bar is the same, but the market and the room are not. They carry the edge.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, an inside day days after a breakout. Is it above the 200-day with the 50-day over it? Take it or pass.
choices: Take it; the lines are stacked
Pass; under the 200-day
Pass; the 50-day is under the 200
questions.answer: Take it; the lines are stacked
questions.why: Take it. Above the 200-day with the 50-day over it, days after a breakout, on light volume. The break came the next session and reached 3R in two days.
questions.lesson_line: Check the lines and the location before the bar. Stacked, after a breakout: that is the spot.

wrong.Pass; under the 200-day: Price sits well above the 200-day here, days after a breakout.
wrong.Pass; the 50-day is under the 200: Look again: the 50-day runs above the 200-day.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. Is the last bar an inside day? Take the break over its high, or pass.
choices: Pass; its high is above yesterday's
Take it; the narrowest day in a week
Take it; the low is inside
questions.answer: Pass; its high is above yesterday's
questions.why: Pass. The high is 0.30% above the prior day's high while the low is 1.26% inside; both ends must be inside. A narrow-range day after a breakout, not an inside day.
questions.lesson_line: Narrow is not inside. The high gives it away.

wrong.Take it; the narrowest day in a week: A narrow day can still poke above yesterday's high. This one did.
wrong.Take it; the low is inside: One end inside is half a definition. The high is above yesterday's.

questions.q: Your call?
choices: Take it; location, stock, market agree
Pass; the bar alone is random
Wait for the close
questions.answer: Take it; location, stock, market agree
questions.why: Take it, at market. The bar alone is near random; the stock, the location and the market carry the edge, and all three agree here. Our Sunday Scans point to this picture: an inside day and a higher low at a rising 20 EMA.
questions.lesson_line: When the stock, the spot and the market all say yes, the quiet day is the door.

wrong.Pass; the bar alone is random: Alone, yes. Here it sits inside a leader's pullback in a Green market. That is the setup.
wrong.Wait for the close: The trigger is the trade over the high, bought at market. Our default does not wait for the close.

questions.story: A clean inside day at a rising 20-day in a leader. Green market, no earnings for weeks, the stop 1.5% under the trigger. At 10:20 the high trades.

questions.q: Breakout whipsaws can be brutal, so the stop is a real order a few cents under the inside day's low.
questions.why: True. Breakout strategies win often, but whipsaws can be brutal. A real stop order, a few cents under the inside day's low, keeps a whipsaw small.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is an appointment, not a debate.
